papers.why: 透過優化學習過程中的引導方式，讓AI用更少資源學會更聰明的推理能力

papers.name: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
papers.zh: 將影片內容轉化為結構化決策的視覺模型
papers.why: 能精準分析影片時間點與文字選項，幫助AI視覺助理更有效率地執行任務

papers.name: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
papers.zh: 讓AI自動生成前後一致的長影片
papers.why: 透過劇本拆解與記憶更新機制，解決長影片容易畫面錯亂的問題

papers.name: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
papers.zh: 結合遊戲紀錄與模擬環境來精進操作技巧
papers.why: 讓AI透過大量模擬與遊戲示範學習，大幅提升遊戲控制能力

papers.name: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
papers.zh: 為結構化決策打造的基礎模型架構
papers.why: 整合多項核心運算設計，讓AI能更快速且準確地做出複雜決策

papers.name: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
papers.zh: 讓電腦學會像真人一樣操作各種軟體介面
papers.why: 整合畫面與程式執行能力，大幅提升電腦代理人處理複雜任務的效率與表現

papers.name: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.zh: 改善多個AI老師同時指導時的衝突問題
papers.why: 協調不同老師的意見來引導學習，避免AI被互相矛盾的指令搞混

papers.name: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
papers.zh: 用真實客戶交辦任務來考驗AI代理人的實力
papers.why: 揭露AI面對模糊需求時的表現落差，有助於突破AI落實到真實應用的最後瓶頸

papers.name: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment
papers.zh: 測試AI把平面的視覺畫面轉成3D旋轉控制的能力
papers.why: 發現現有模型在三維空間推理上與人類有很大差距，為空間智慧提供評測標準

papers.name: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
papers.zh: 教導AI助理自我反省以修正錯誤指令
papers.why: 讓AI在面對工具出錯或使用者修正時懂得自我檢討，大幅提升互動的準確度

papers.name: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
papers.zh: 能在不改動模型參數下自我進化的AI系統
papers.why: 讓AI助理透過回饋與演化機制持續變聰明，不需要重新訓練模型就能自我升級

papers.name: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching
papers.zh: 用一次性分類快速完成空間推理的決策模型
papers.why: 大幅提升運作速度與準確度，解決傳統模型反應太慢的問題

papers.name: Learning Where to Split: Dynamic Band Splitting for Audio Source Separation
papers.zh: 會自動調整頻率分界線的聲音分離技術
papers.why: 在不增加運算負擔的前提下，把混音分離得更乾淨、品質更好

papers.name: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
papers.zh: 讓AI在大型3D城市中像真人一樣主動探索
papers.why: 結合視覺語言與強化學習，不用預先標註就能在龐大城市場景中快速定位

secwords.src: SEC EDGAR 全文檢索（10-K、10-Q、8-K 含附件，計文件數）

items.title: Getting real about AI: How AI agents are changing the economics of software engineering
items.desc: Cognition co-founder and President Russell Kaplan explains why the next frontier of AI in software engineering is about more than writing code faster and what it takes to turn autonomous agents into measurable business value.

items.title: What is a forward-deployed engineer?
items.desc: Forward-deployed engineers work inside another company’s own systems. Three McKinsey leaders explain how FDEs help companies derive impact from AI.

items.title: The judgment bottleneck: Balancing AI and human speeds in strategy
items.desc: Analysis now runs on AI time, but judgment still runs on human time. Three moves can help turn AI’s speed into better strategy decisions.

items.title: Strengthening supply chains behind US semiconductors
items.desc: New research maps hidden upstream dependencies in the US semiconductor supply chain and outlines potential mitigation strategies to make the ecosystem more resilient.

items.title: Voices on Planning: The AI-powered future of supply chain
items.desc: The shift from software as a service to AI-enabled planning could move decision-making from fixed cycles to real time, but success will require the right governance, expertise, and operating model.

items.title: The AI value curve: The economics of applying AI to existing work
items.desc: Many organizations are still measuring AI adoption instead of value. The AI value curve helps identify where AI’s automation potential can be deployed most cost-effectively.

items.title: Rewiring capital projects to boost construction productivity
items.desc: McKinsey’s Capital Excellence experts discuss how AI and technology can boost construction productivity, address labor shortages, and accelerate delivery of complex capital projects.

items.title: What does AI really cost?
items.desc: Moving an AI tool from pilot to production can nearly quadruple its cost. Three McKinsey experts explain why—and how to tell whether it’s worth it.

items.title: Why the future of capital projects belongs to digital and AI-enabled teams
items.desc: Digital and AI are changing the way capital projects are selected, designed, procured, built, and steered. Leaders are moving beyond pilots to rewire how projects are planned and delivered.

items.title: The AI operating system: A new way for CEOs to run the enterprise
items.desc: An AI operating system can become an enterprise’s “second brain,” but only if CEOs rethink how management itself evolves.

items.title: McKinsey research shows AI creating more jobs than automation displaces — but 11 million American workers will need help this decade
items.desc: While debates about AI’s impact on the workforce dominate headlines, the biggest challenge ahead will be helping workers find the most direct pathway into growing jobs, write Eric Kutcher and Tanguy Catlin in Fortune.

items.title: As the world order turns, leading companies are keeping pace. Here’s how
items.desc: Leading companies are tracking six emerging patterns of geopolitical change and realigning their businesses to achieve resilience, seize growth, and build competitive advantage.

items.title: Why AI’s easiest wins are misleading CEOs
AI is changing work. Now it has to change the organization
items.desc: The first phase of enterprise AI put powerful new tools in people’s hands. Capturing the larger opportunity from agentic AI will require leaders to rethink the shape of the organization itself.

items.title: Scaling AI inference
items.desc: Inference is reshaping AI economics, infrastructure architectures, and investment priorities across the semiconductor ecosystem.

items.title: Pause, pivot, or accelerate: SaaS in the age of agentic AI
items.desc: Agentic AI is reshaping the case for modernization in insurance. Leaders from Guidewire, Bessemer Venture Partners, and SAP discuss how insurers can respond, considering their existing commitments.

items.title: Siemens’s next reinvention: An interview with Cedrik Neike
items.desc: As technology transforms the factory floor, industrial companies are confronting a broader question: What will it take to lead the next era of manufacturing?

items.title: The bank’s digital twin: The future of nonfinancial risk management
items.desc: The risk function’s fundamental purpose has not changed, but the nature of the risks, the pace at which they materialize, and the tools available to manage them have.

items.title: Modernizing for the mission: An interview with Jamie Wolff
items.desc: The National Nuclear Security Administration’s CIO shares that modernization means rebuilding infrastructure, data, and talent at once—while keeping the mission and a relentless pace of change in mind.

items.title: The CEO’s singular impact on the success—or failure—of AI in organizations
items.desc: There are certain aspects of the AI opportunity that chief executives cannot hand off to others—raising the organization’s ambition, rearchitecting how it works, and resetting its culture.

items.title: Workforce in motion: Skills and pathways to future jobs in the United States
items.desc: AI, automation, and broader structural trends are accelerating the reallocation of work across the US economy. Capturing its benefits requires developing new professional pathways and skills, and reducing barriers between declining and growing occupations.

items.title: The next phase of government AI economics
items.desc: Subsidized AI pilots are expiring as usage explodes. Here’s how US public sector leaders can treat AI spend as a managed category before the bill arrives.

items.title: Make life better: Mikhail Lomtadze’s customer-first philosophy
items.desc: Mikhail Lomtadze, cofounder and CEO of Kaspi, believes the only measure that matters is whether Kaspi makes customers’ lives better or not—and why that single conviction changes everything else.

items.title: AI is changing how we work. Is your organization ready?
items.desc: As AI reshapes roles, leaders face a bigger question: how to rethink jobs, teams, and the way work gets done in a fundamentally different era.

items.title: The AI-powered future of care
items.desc: AI won’t replace clinicians, but it can improve quality, increase access, and reshape the workforce, payments, and patient volumes. Today, AI can perform some 16 to 22 percent of US outpatient care.

items.title: Democratized superintelligence is coming: The world needs to get ready
items.desc: Bret Taylor, Sierra cofounder and OpenAI chair, believes AI’s near-term cybersecurity risks are real but solvable, and its greater power lies in delivering the world’s best knowledge to everyone.

items.title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer
items.desc: AI could improve both safety and productivity by anticipating problems before they arise, detecting worker fatigue, and automating dangerous tasks.

items.title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries
items.desc: Embedding the latest AI and technology within day-to-day operations is transforming maintenance from a cost center into a significant driver of value.

items.title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon
items.desc: As India’s economy continues to ramp up, insurers have an opportunity to capture value by improving productivity, modernizing operating models, and scaling technology and AI across the enterprise.

items.title: Rewiring procurement in resources: Making judgment an enduring asset
items.desc: For procurement leaders in the resources sector, using AI to codify the function’s category expertise does not just capture more value—it turns hard-won judgment into a compounded, durable advantage.

items.title: Ready to ramp? How US manufacturers can scale at pace
items.desc: US manufacturers have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to reshore the production of critical and at-risk goods, but to do so, they will need to aggressively ramp up production from today’s levels.

items.title: WIRED: The AI playbook top companies use
items.desc: WIRED’s Katie Drummond talks with McKinsey’s Dan Swan about why capturing AI’s full potential requires companies to move beyond experimentation and fundamentally rewire their businesses.

items.title: The economics of AI
items.desc: AI is getting more expensive for companies. As rising token usage and workflow complexity make costs harder to predict, leaders need new ways to manage AI economics.

items.title: AI drug discovery: Focusing on what matters most
items.desc: AI is accelerating drug discovery, but investment has concentrated in molecule design—the stage with the best data and clearest tools. The industry’s real constraint lies elsewhere: identifying and validating the right disease mechanism.

items.title: Novartis’s Christian Diehl on scaling AI beyond the demo
items.desc: Novartis’s chief data and digital officer for biomedical research explains how data platform investments are paying off in AI safety prediction, generative chemistry, and faster translation.

items.title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story
items.desc: AI is fueling unprecedented semiconductor growth while upending long-standing industry dynamics and shifting the sources of value.

items.title: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows
items.desc: Organizations must redesign workflows to realize value from AI, but the challenge is where to begin. An opportunity lies between workflow steps, where work passes between teams and systems.

items.title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity
items.desc: As enterprises shift from experimenting with models to redesigning workflows, new research suggests Europe could be well-positioned for this new AI application era.

items.title: Why medtechs can’t afford to overlook customer experience
items.desc: Customer experience is a competitive imperative for medtechs. To create a durable advantage, it must be designed into products from day one, not added as a post-sale service.

items.title: Meesho: Making e-commerce everyone’s business
items.desc: Scaling an e-commerce start-up in India’s dispersed markets is challenging, but innovation, patience, and passionately solving hard problems have enabled Meesho’s founders to succeed.

items.title: For CPG companies, agentic AI’s real payoff is growth
items.desc: As the relationship between consumer-packaged-goods companies and retailers becomes more complex, agentic AI can recapture lost sales. But are leaders ready to harness the technology’s power?

items.title: State of Consumer Africa 2026: Meeting the pragmatic shopper
items.desc: Household budgets in Africa are tight and channels increasingly fragmented. Four trends are redefining how consumers discover, decide, and spend, and how consumer-facing companies can respond.

items.title: How leaders are turning AI into growth
items.desc: Nearly 90 percent of companies are investing in AI, but only 6 percent see material impact. The difference is in how they approach it.

items.title: LATAM’s reinvention at 35,000 feet
items.desc: Partnering with McKinsey, the airline rewired its organization to make digital and AI core parts of the business—transforming the passenger experience, accelerating growth, and unlocking new levels of operations performance.

items.title: America’s next workforce challenge: Building pathways to better jobs
items.desc: Over the next decade, AI, automation, and economic forces like demographic aging will set off the largest workforce restructuring in history, writes Kweilin Ellingrud in Forbes.

items.title: Energy security in an age of disruption
items.desc: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives, write Diego Hernandez Diaz, Luciano Di Fiori, and Tiago Devesa in Project Syndicate.

items.title: Navigating the new normal: Building resilience in fuel retail trading
items.desc: Commodity markets have entered a new era of persistent volatility. For fuel retailers, this is a chance to strengthen resilience and unlock value, but only with strategic investment and a shift in mindset.

items.title: Convenience or discovery: Which mission will your store serve?
items.desc: As AI reshapes how consumers browse, shop, and buy, retailers must choose a mission for every location—and commit to it.

items.title: Billion-dollar beauty: The odds of scaling a breakout brand
items.desc: Our new analysis reveals the odds of reaching $1 billion in sales—and how the paths to that milestone differ by category and ownership.

items.title: The new growth mandate: A conversation with LinkedIn CMO Jessica Jensen
items.desc: At Cannes Lions 2026, LinkedIn CMO Jessica Jensen and McKinsey senior partner Dianne Esber discussed what it takes to turn AI from experimentation into a catalyst for growth.

items.title: Author Talks: The business of owning a sports team
items.desc: How does business ownership compare with owning a sports team? Baltimore Orioles owner David M. Rubenstein explains the leadership mindset, culture building, and long-term thinking that team ownership requires.

items.title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices
items.desc: Travelers’ discovery and booking journeys have been reshaped. How can travel players show up at every turn on the path from search to certainty?

items.title: China Auto Consumer Insights 2026: Consumers set the pace
items.desc: The 10th edition of McKinsey’s automotive consumer survey: China’s car buyers reveal where value is heading—and why the road ahead is exciting for consumers everywhere.

items.title: The CMO as impact driver: A conversation with Genentech CMO Zoë Lazarre
items.desc: Genentech’s chief marketing officer discusses AI, the future of marketing, patient trust, and why growth depends as much on culture as technology.

items.title: Place, purpose, and the path to economic mobility
items.desc: Where you live shapes far more than you’d think. New research points to how community, place, and connection relate to getting ahead.

items.title: Asset management 2026: Plenty for the few?
items.desc: A golden age for the industry is becoming a golden age for a smaller group of asset managers.

items.title: The six strategy roles a CEO must not delegate
items.desc: Strategy is a team sport, but the value it creates ultimately depends on the CEO’s involvement.

items.title: The playbook for seeing around geopolitical corners
items.desc: From black swans to gray rhinos, geopolitical shocks are multiplying. Here’s the tool kit smart leaders use to see them coming.

items.title: Shapers and Founders: Understanding the owner mindset
items.desc: Marrying Eastern philosophy and Western management culture has given many of Asia’s owner-CEOs a unique edge in growing their businesses.

items.title: Medtech needs more than a market rotation to win back investors
items.desc: With industry performance plateauing, medtech leaders must earn back investor trust with fresh strategies and better execution.

items.title: Author Talks: Rana Foroohar on a new ‘great game’ in the Arctic
items.desc: From shipping and rare earths to energy and security, the Arctic is gaining importance in the global economy. The Financial Times’ Rana Foroohar explores its role in a new era of great-power competition.

items.title: Using production rates to excel at executing construction projects
items.desc: As construction productivity stagnates, companies can stand out by employing granular, achievable rates of production to optimize schedules, improve productivity, and make delivery predictable.

items.title: Shareholder activism is changing. Are companies ready?
items.desc: Boards and CEOs can build value-creation plans that withstand and even benefit from shareholder activist scrutiny.

items.title: America’s next growth opportunity: An investment-ready heartland
items.desc: With a more coordinated approach, smaller cities in the middle of the country could generate trillions of dollars in added economic output.

items.title: The cash hiding in plain sight
items.desc: Companies often have significant opportunities to unlock cash. Four practices can help CFOs free it up.

items.title: Evidence over hype: New York’s path to a healthy-longevity economy
items.desc: A McKinsey survey finds that New Yorkers prioritize healthy longevity—and spend accordingly.

items.title: How to drive transformations with rigor
items.desc: McKinsey research finds that companies executing transformations with rigor are much more likely to meet overall organizational transformation goals. Chris Hagedorn, Preeya Mody, and Michel Morenville join us to discuss what rigor really means in the context of transformation and how to embed it throughout the process, from setting the aspiration, to mobilization, to delivering impact.

items.title: Global Economics Intelligence executive summary, August 2026
items.desc: Public debt and search for growth exercise minds of economists and policymakers as US debt hits record high; inflation fueled by energy supply uncertainty limits room for maneuver on interest rates.

items.title: Economic conditions outlook, September 2026
items.desc: Executives’ economic pessimism has eased since June, but they remain cautious. Negative views continue to be more common than positive ones, and expectations for the next six months are mixed.

items.title: Author Talks: Can you fulfill your ambition and compose a life?
items.desc: Mayfield’s former Chief Marketing Officer Kamini Ramani draws on Indian women leaders’ experiences in corporate America to bring a culturally rooted lens to ambition, resilience, and leadership.

items.title: Leading when change feels threatening
items.desc: Fear and change can go hand in hand. Executives who understand this can significantly improve their odds of transformation success, while the executives who don’t risk sabotaging their change programs.

items.title: Powering through uncertainty: A talk with former US Energy Secretary Ernest Moniz
items.desc: The physicist and policymaker says the coming decade will be defined by a race for electrons—and that nuclear power, grid investment, and new public–private models will be part of the picture.
cats: Insights on Electric Power & Natural Gas

items.title: The future of healthy living: A $16.4 trillion opportunity
items.desc: New McKinsey Health Institute analysis finds that addressing modifiable risk factors could add 12 years to healthy life expectancy at birth and add nearly 9 percent to the global economy by 2050.

items.title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply
items.desc: A new era of increased demand and constrained supply is fundamentally changing the global transformer market and reshaping decision-making across the value chain.
cats: Insights on Electric Power & Natural Gas

items.title: Social care referral networks: Improving health in rural communities
items.desc: Six design dimensions can help states stand up social care referral networks that meaningfully improve health outcomes for Medicaid members in rural and underserved communities.

items.title: Author Talks: How to turn hope into action
items.desc: What compels us to act when we see a problem? Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation CEO Jim Bildner reflects on social entrepreneurship, personal loss, and how hope can move us to act.

items.title: Here’s why some US industrial companies achieve higher multiples
items.desc: Not every industrial company in a high-growth market earns a higher valuation. The biggest winners consistently combine four management actions.

items.title: Why transformations stall—and where only CEOs make the difference
items.desc: Five common behavioral patterns can cause change efforts to falter. Know the warning signs—and what to do about them.

items.title: Aftershocks: Energy security beyond the Strait of Hormuz crisis
items.desc: The energy system has proven surprisingly resilient, but shock absorbers are thinning. Energy security has no easy exits but room to maneuver.

items.title: 海外油價飆破110美元
items.body: 布蘭特原油自5月以來首度觸及110美元。Google搜尋出現100+搜尋量，報導指遇襲恐推升全球物價，直接加劇台灣能源進口成本與通膨壓力。

items.title: 備轉容量率大增至28.14%

items.title: 仁武人口公司雙增且醫療診所淨增
items.body: 高雄市仁武區近 12 個月人口淨流入820人，診所新開5家、歇業1家，淨增4家。新設公司從上月24家增至本月35家，月增%達46%，類別集中在餐飲與設計創意。
items.why: 近 12 個月人口淨流入全台第 21（高雄市第 1）

weekly.headline: 生產與外銷維持紅燈高溫，內需消費呈防禦收縮，單身與寵物需求未獲供給滿足。

dirs.t: 外銷與科技製造持續過熱
dirs.why: 外銷訂單年增61.9%，製造業PMI達63.4，上市櫃電子通路營收年增90.2%，半導體年增59.3%，維持高檔。

dirs.t: 民生終端消費轉趨保守防禦
dirs.why: PPI年增16.75%高於CPI的2.04%，信用卡百貨較整體慢5.4個百分點，副業搜尋暴增335%，民眾尋求開源。
src: 主題鏈（需求 vs 供給）

dirs.t: 新設企業動能衰退零售萎縮
dirs.why: 公司新設年增-7.9%、解散增9.8%，淨新設降至2110家；批發及零售業淨減118家最多，商號擴張明顯降溫。

gaps.t: 寵物照護服務與專利供給不足
gaps.why: 高齡人口占20.62%，毛孩搜尋+19且維基+31，立法推動寵物食品法，但商標-23、新店-11，供給落後需求。
src: 主題鏈（需求 vs 供給）

gaps.t: 單身獨居生活配套未獲填補
gaps.why: 平均每戶降至2.34人，獨居搜尋+45、小宅搜尋+10，但小宅商標-10、新店-14，獨居新店-2，實體供給未跟上。
src: 主題鏈（需求 vs 供給）

risks.t: 生產成本難以轉嫁擠壓利潤
risks.why: PPI年增16.75%與CPI年增2.04%差距逾14個百分點，加上全球油脂與穀物漲逾17%，廠商成本壓力沉重。

risks.t: 美股尾部風險升溫衝擊外需
risks.why: VIX雖僅15.2，但美股SKEW指數高達154偏離常態，顯示市場避險情緒增強，存在外部修正風險。

watch.t: 預計公布之2026-09消費者物價指數CPI年增率
watch.check: 高於2.3%為物價反彈且判斷正確，低於2.0%為持續趨緩且判斷錯誤

watch.t: 台北蔬菜批發籃子比近兩週均價變動率
watch.check: 比值轉負或小於0%為菜價回落且預測正確，高於+3.0%為續漲且預測錯誤

weekly.vs_last: 外需強消費冷及副業需求被證實；批發零售淨減顯示內需實體比上週預估更保守。

past.headline: 景氣強但民生消費偏冷，科技動能高，寵物與獨老需求未獲供給滿足。
